I've been farming these 50 mu in Quzhou County for 30 years now. I'm 52, finished middle school, and farming is what I know. Our household has seven people — my wife and I, my elderly father, my two sons, plus one daughter-in-law and a grandchild. Both my sons work off-farm at a construction site in Handan, so they send money home, but they're not around for the busy season. That means my wife, my father, and I do the day-to-day work, but I have to hire labor when things get intense.

Last year my wheat did about 900 jin per mu, and maize did about 1,000 jin per mu. The soil on my land is pretty average — not the best in the village, but not the worst either. This year I'm not changing much. The extension technician came by and suggested I try a new wheat variety, but I've been growing this improved Jimai type for three years and it does fine. Why fix what isn't broken? For wheat, I'll plant around October 8th. I'll put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base before planting, then topdress with 18 kg of urea per mu at jointing in late March. The extension guy says 15 kg urea is enough, but I always add a bit more — losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. I'll irrigate three times: winter irrigation after planting, one at green-up in spring, and one at jointing or heading depending on the rain. Electricity for the well pump costs about 25 yuan per mu each time, so I won't do four like some of the big business farms.

For maize, the window after wheat harvest is brutal — sometimes only five or six days. I hire a combine for wheat, then run the rotary harrow once and get the maize in the ground immediately around June 12th. I buy fresh hybrid seed every year; it's about 38 yuan per mu but you can't save hybrid seed. Base fertilizer is 40 kg of compound per mu at planting, then 20 kg of urea per mu at the big-flare stage in late July. Maize gets two irrigations — one around jointing and one at ear stage. Summer rain helps, but I've learned not to count on it.

I hire about 10 days of labor for wheat harvest and 12 days for maize planting and harvest. Day laborers want 150 yuan a day now. All told, my inputs and hired labor will cost about 33,000 yuan this year. That's a lot of cash upfront, but with wheat and maize prices holding steady, and my sons' off-farm income giving us a buffer, I don't need to cut corners and risk a bad year. Better to spend the money and get a reliable crop than try to save a few yuan and regret it.
